main_theorem.statement_math: \text{Suppose that Assumption 2 holds. Choose the stepsize }\eta\le \frac{1}{L\left(1+\sqrt{\frac{1-p}{pb'}}\right)},\text{ minibatch size }b=n,\text{ secondary minibatch size }b'<b,\text{ and probability }p_t\equiv p\in(0,1].\text{ Then the number of iterations performed by PAGE sufficient for finding an }\epsilon\text{-approximate solution (i.e., }\mathbb{E}[\|\nabla f(\hat{x}_T)\|]\le \epsilon\text{) of nonconvex finite-sum problem (2) can be bounded by }T=\frac{2\Delta_0L}{\epsilon^2}\left(1+\sqrt{\frac{1-p}{pb'}}\right).\text{ Moreover, the number of stochastic gradient computations (i.e., gradient complexity) is }\#\mathrm{grad}=b+T(pb+(1-p)b')=b+\frac{2\Delta_0L}{\epsilon^2}\left(1+\sqrt{\frac{1-p}{pb'}}\right)(pb+(1-p)b').
main_theorem.rate: Theorem 1 gives T = (2 Delta_0 L / epsilon^2)(1 + sqrt((1-p)/(p b'))) iterations and gradient complexity b + T(pb + (1-p)b'); Corollary 2 chooses p=b'/(b+b') and b'<=sqrt(b) to obtain O(n + sqrt(n)/epsilon^2).
main_theorem.measure: Expected gradient norm E[||nabla f(xhat_T)||] for the random output iterate.

proof.description: From Assumption 2 and Lemma 1, f is L-smooth. Applying Lemma 2 to the PAGE update x^{t+1}:=x^t-eta g^t gives the one-step descent inequality.
Invoke Lemma 3 to bound the next estimator error by the old estimator error and the PAGE step length.
Set p_t equiv p, add (14) to eta/(2p) times (15), and take expectation. This is the expanded add-and-scale inequality before like terms are collected.
Collect the old estimator-error coefficients and the step-norm coefficients in the expanded inequality.
Use the stepsize condition to make the coefficient of ||x^{t+1}-x^t||^2 nonnegative, so the negative step-norm term can be dropped.
proof.ref: Last inequality in Eq. (19) and Eq. (20), p. 14

abla f(x^t)\|^2- rac{\eta}{2}\|
abla f(x^t)\|^2ight],\quad  rac{1}{2\eta}- rac{L}{2}- rac{(1-p)\eta L^2}{2pb'}\ge 0\quad	ext{by choosing stepsize}\quad \eta\le  rac{1}{L\left(1+\sqrt{ rac{1-p}{pb'}}ight)}.

proof.description: Define the Lyapunov function Phi_t using the function gap and scaled gradient-estimator error.
Rewrite (19) in terms of Phi_t and Phi_{t+1}.
Sum the Lyapunov descent inequality from t=0 to T-1 to telescope the Phi terms.

Identify the initial Lyapunov value. Since the theorem sets b=n, Line 1 computes the full gradient g^0=nabla f(x^0), so the estimator-error term in Phi_0 vanishes and the paper writes Phi_0=f(x^0)-f^*=Delta_0.
Use nonnegativity of the terminal Lyapunov value: f(x^T)-f^* is nonnegative by the definition of f^*, and the squared estimator-error term is nonnegative.
Drop the nonnegative E[Phi_T] term from the telescoped inequality and substitute Phi_0=Delta_0, deriving the summed squared-gradient bound consumed by the output step.
Use the PAGE output rule that \hat{x}_T is uniformly chosen from \{x^t\}_{t\in[T]} to divide the summed squared-gradient bound by T and obtain (23).
Set the iteration count using the reciprocal stepsize bound from (20).
Apply Jensen's inequality to pass from the second-moment output bound to the expected norm guarantee.
Combine the iteration bound with the expected number of stochastic gradients per PAGE iteration and include the initial minibatch cost.

key_lemmas.name: Lemma2_descent_with_inexact_gradient
key_lemmas.ref: Lemma 2 / Eq. (11), p. 12
key_lemmas.statement_math: \text{Suppose that function }f\text{ is }L\text{-smooth and let }x^{t+1}:=x^t-\eta g^t.\text{ Then for any }g^t\in\mathbb{R}^d\text{ and }\eta>0,\text{ we have }f(x^{t+1})\le f(x^t)-\frac{\eta}{2}\|\nabla f(x^t)\|^2-\left(\frac{1}{2\eta}-\frac{L}{2}\right)\|x^{t+1}-x^t\|^2+\frac{\eta}{2}\|g^t-\nabla f(x^t)\|^2.
key_lemmas.role: Converts a PAGE primal update with an inexact gradient estimator into the descent inequality (14).

proof.description: Define the exact-gradient comparison point and apply the L-smoothness inequality (8) at y=x^{t+1}. This uses Lemma 2's local hypothesis that f is L-smooth, not the average-smoothness-to-smoothness conversion from Lemma 1.
Split the inner product into the estimator error part and the estimator part while preserving the upper-bound chain from the preceding line.
Use x^{t+1}=x^t-eta g^t to rewrite the estimator inner product as a negative squared step length.
Expand -eta<gradient error,g^t> by writing g^t as nabla f(x^t) minus the estimator error.
Replace the cross term by the comparison-point expression involving x^{t+1}-bar{x}^{t+1} and x^t-bar{x}^{t+1}.
Use the polarization identity to rewrite the comparison-point cross term as a difference of three squared norms.
Substitute x^{t+1}-bar{x}^{t+1}=-eta(g^t-nabla f(x^t)) and x^t-bar{x}^{t+1}=eta nabla f(x^t).
Collect the coefficients of the true gradient norm, the step norm, and the estimator-error norm to obtain the displayed inequality (11).

main_theorem.statement_math: \text{Corollary 2 (Optimal result for problem (2)) Suppose that Assumption 2 holds.
